articles.title: New York City man shot in car with child present by ICE agents, mayor says
articles.description: US immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in ​his car with a child present in the Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses. Federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since Republican President Donald Trump returned to office, 7 fatally, sparking protests across ​the US.

articles.title: Russian strike on buses kills at least 30 in frontline Ukrainian city
articles.description: Ukraine on Thursday accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians after 30 people were killed when two buses were blown up in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, in one of the deadliest attacks in weeks. President Volodymyr Zelensky vowed that it "will not go unanswered" after photos posted by local authorities showed the burnt-out metal shell of the vehicles, with bodies and debris strewn across the road. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

articles.title: Les Etats-Unis imposent des sanctions contre la CPI, qui réagit en critiquant une « attaque contre l’Etat de droit »
articles.description: L’Union européenne a déploré vendredi les sanctions « profondément regrettables » des Etats-Unis contre la Cour pénale internationale, et a promis d’aider l’institution à poursuivre ses missions. Cette annonce intervient quelques heures après que l’ancienne juge sud-africaine Navi Pillay a été récompensée du prix Nobel de la paix

articles.title: Le Pen's top ally Bardella faces fresh claims he sought to cover up past anti-Semitic comments
articles.description: France's far-right National Rally leader Jordan Bardella deleted data from a former activist Facebook account as soon as allegations surfaced that he wrote anti-Semitic comments in his youth, French investigative weekly Le Canard enchaîné said Friday, piling pressure on the top ally of presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen.

articles.title: International Criminal Court faces 'test of resilience' as US imposes sweeping sanctions
articles.description: The Trump administration has imposed sweeping new sanctions on the International Criminal Court as part of its campaign to dismantle what it describes as a "rogue" tribunal, threatening to cripple its operations. Following the move, ⁠the European Union said it was "ready to take any necessary measures to enable the court to carry out its work".

articles.title: Lawsuits blame Fox News for deaths of journalists in Ukraine
articles.description: This week, FRANCE 24's media show Scoop revisits a fatal assignment for a Fox News team in Ukraine. On March 14, 2022, a Russian strike hit the crew reporting near the capital Kyiv. Reporter Benjamin Hall was seriously injured and two other journalists were killed. The journalists' families are suing Fox, saying the network put the story ahead of its people. Our guest is NPR's David Folkenflik.

articles.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les Etats-Unis mènent des discussions avec l’Ukraine lors d’une rencontre en Floride à laquelle ont également été conviés les Européens
articles.description: La délégation ukrainienne doit rencontrer Jared Kushner et Steve Witkoff, émissaires de Donald Trump, pour cette réunion qui « devrait durer deux jours », a affirmé Volodymyr Zelensky à des journalistes avant les pourparlers.

articles.title: French high school students react to Education Minister’s measures
articles.description: In response to the massive high school student protests in France, Education Minister Édouard Geffray announced emergency measures on Thursday, October 8. Some students reacted to these measures in interviews with France 24.

articles.title: India protests grow over Election Commission mistrust
articles.description: In this edition of Access Asia, we find out why multiple protests have broken out in India after an investigation by The Indian Express raised concerns about the integrity of the country's Election Commission. Journalist Faye D'Souza joins us to unpack how Narendra Modi's government is facing mounting pressure from the political opposition and the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party. She also discusses the wider sense of discontent in India.

articles.title: Morocco and Senegal await AFCON final verdict after arbitration hearing
articles.description: Thursday saw the Court of Arbitration for Sport hold a long-awaited hearing in Lausanne, as sport's highest court considered Senegal's appeal over the decision to award Morocco this year's Africa Cup of Nations title. While Senegal won the match on the pitch in Rabat 10 months ago, the Confederation of African Football later overturned the result because the Lions of Teranga had left the pitch in protest mid-game before coming back on. The three-judge panel is expected to issue a verdict soon.

articles.title: Residents of Ukraine's Kramatorsk forced to flee as drone strikes intensify
articles.description: The city of Kramatorsk, in eastern Ukraine, is increasingly coming under Russian attack. For those who have stayed behind, the threat from drones and shelling has become a daily reality. Many have resisted leaving their homes, despite the growing danger – but now, more and more residents are being forced to flee. Our colleagues at France 2 followed an evacuation from the city and witnessed first-hand the dangers that residents face.

articles.title: Guerre en Ukraine : les récentes frappes russes ont causé des «dommages considérables» au réseau électrique, selon Volodymyr Zelensky
articles.description: Les autorités ukrainiennes ont instauré ces derniers jours des coupures d’électricité d’urgence et des restrictions dans plusieurs régions après des frappes russes sur les infrastructures énergétiques.

articles.title: Primaire à gauche : comparez les propositions des cinq candidats

articles.title: Eritrea and Ethiopia accuse each other of provoking war as Tigray rebels retreat
articles.description: Ethiopia and Eritrea on Friday accused each other of starting a "war of agresson" days after the two countries severed diplomatic ties. Ethiopian officals estimate that up to 8,000 Eritrean soldiers are present in Tigray supporting rebels who last month launched attacks against federal forces.

articles.title: Senegal, Morocco to get AFCON title verdict within days
articles.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Thursday opened its hearing into Senegal's appeal against being stripped of the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title in favour of Morocco. The hearing in Lausanne comes almost 10 months after Pape Gueye's extra-time goal gave Senegal victory over the tournament hosts following a chaotic finish to normal time. But in March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title.

articles.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le fondateur du canal Telegram Rybar, important vecteur de la propagande du Kremlin, arrêté au Monténégro
articles.description: Mikhaïl Zvintchouk et plusieurs ressortissants russes ont été interpellés à Risan, au Monténégro. Le premier ministre monténégrin a salué une « opération réussie », évoquant des tentatives d’ingérence hybride et de déstabilisation, sans plus de détails. Mikhaïl Zvintchouk, visé par des sanctions européennes et britanniques, est suivi par plus de 1,5 million d’abonnés.

articles.title: Quand l’IA devient le guide de voyage pour planifier ses vacances : « Le secteur touristique est à un point de bascule »
articles.description: De l’inspiration à la réservation, l’intelligence artificielle s’immisce à toutes les étapes des vacances. Hôtels, agences ou destinations cherchent à ne pas rater le virage. At Issey Miyake, it's about sensuality rooted in the Japanese concept of Ma, the space that bridges the gap between fabric and skin. It's a similar story at Yohji Yamamoto who, at 83, is still on the hunt for emotions.

articles.title: En Syrie, le long chemin vers la justice et la vérité pour les victimes de la guerre
articles.description: Près de deux ans après la chute de Bachar Al-Assad, entre 200 000 et 300 000 Syriens sont toujours portés disparus. Le nouveau pouvoir a mis en place des commissions pour enquêter sur ces crimes et une justice transitionnelle, mais la société civile s’inquiète d’un cadre juridique encore flou.

articles.title: Falling test scores in schools startle EU countries: Why are standards going down?
articles.description: It has been dubbed "the PISA shock". Countries that had been used to their school pupils performing well in test scores are seeing a plunge in standards. The PISA test is an international assessment led by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), which measures how well 15‑year‑olds in over 80 countries apply reading, mathematics and science skills to real‑world problems. articles.description: C'est une "information fausse", a rétorqué vendredi l'entourage du président du RN, annonçant qu'une plainte en diffamation "sera déposée dans les prochaines heures".

articles.title: Four astronauts return to Earth after eight months in space
articles.description: An astronaut crew that carried out an eight-month mission aboard the International Space Station splashed down as planned Thursday off the coast of California. During the mission, Sophie Adenot became the first French female astronaut to venture outside the space station for a spacewalk. In all, she undertook three spacewalks on August 18 and 25, and September 1.

articles.title: Callum Turner's new film sparkles at Dinard Film Festival
